## Why This Is Asked
This tests ability to design cross-cloud Terraform patterns with strict data residency, multi-tenant isolation, and robust gatekeeping.

## Key Concepts
- Terraform provider aliases across AWS and GCP

- OPA policy integration for plan gating

```hcl
# region allowlist for both clouds
variable "region_allowlist" {
  type = map(list(string))
  default = {
    aws = ["us-east-1","us-west-2"]
    gcp = ["us-central1","us-east1"]
  }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test the OPA policy locally?
- How would you extend to support new clouds?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to scale environments with for_each while reusing a wrapper module, plus enforce governance via a CI gate.

## Key Concepts
- Terraform for_each over a map to create multiple subnets
- Local validations to ensure CIDR uniqueness
- Reusing a shared module with environment tagging
- CI gate with GitHub Actions that blocks prod-touching changes

## Code Example
```javascript
variable "team_subnets" {
  type = map(string)
  default = {
    Alpha = "10.0.1.0/24",
    Beta  = "10.0.2.0/24",
    Gamma = "10.0.3.0/24"
  }
}
locals {
  cidrs = [for _, cidr in var.team_subnets : cidr]
}
validation "cidr_uniqueness" {
  condition = length(distinct(local.cidrs)) == length(local.cidrs)
  error_message = "Subnets CIDRs must be unique"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you detect overlapping CIDRs beyond simple duplicates?
- How would you extend the gate to also verify minimum tag coverage on new resources?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests a practical cross-repo governance pattern for feature flags and ensures drift-detection in CI before apply.

## Key Concepts

- Terraform modules with for_each
- jsondecode from governance JSON via a data source
- CI gating with policy checks (OPA/Sentinel) and pre-apply validation
- Idempotent flag application and per-env overrides

## Code Example

```terraform
data "aws_s3_bucket_object" "flags" {
  bucket = var.gov_bucket
  key    = "flags/${var.env}.json"
}
locals {
  flags = jsondecode(data.aws_s3_bucket_object.flags.body)
}
resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "feature" {
  for_each = local.flags
  name     = "/feature/${each.key}"
  type     = "String"
  value    = tostring(each.value)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test this gating across accounts and environments?
- How would you handle removal of flags or flag value updates without breaking environments?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of gating Terraform changes with feature flags in a multi-env setup, plus per-env state management and metadata propagation.

## Key Concepts
- plan-time gates
- per-env state backends
- wrapper modules for metadata propagation
- feature flag management

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
FEAT=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /flags/feature_network --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value -o text)
if [[ "$ENV" == "prod" && "$FEAT" != "enabled" ]]; then
  echo "Prod network changes blocked"; exit 1
fi
```

- How to migrate backends without downtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates the ability to design cross-cloud Terraform abstractions with proper governance, policy enforcement, and CI controls—essential skills for managing multi-cloud infrastructure at scale.

## Key Concepts

- Cloud-agnostic module design using provider aliases and conditional logic
- Per-tenant tagging for cost allocation and resource isolation
- Policy-as-code using OPA for access control and compliance
- CI gating with GitHub Actions to enforce change management controls

## Code Example

```hcl
# providers.tf
provider "aws" {
  alias  = "aws"
  region = var.cloud == "aws" ? var.region : null
}

provider "google" {
  alias  = "google"
  project = var.cloud == "gcp" ? var.project : null
  region  = var.cloud == "gcp" ? var.region : null
}
```

```hcl
# main.tf
locals {
  provider = var.cloud == "aws" ? "aws.aws" : "google.google"
}

resource "aws_eks_cluster" "this" {
  count = var.cloud == "aws" ? 1 : 0
  # ...
  vpc_config {
    subnet_ids = var.subnets
  }
  tags = var.tags
}

resource "google_container_cluster" "this" {
  count = var.cloud == "gcp" ? 1 : 0
  # ...
  subnetwork = var.subnets[0]
  resource_labels = var.tags
}
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions workflow
gate-prod:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Check PR label
      if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      run: |
        labels=$(echo '${{ join(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, ',') }}')
        if [[ "$labels" != *"allow-prod-change"* ]]; then
          echo "::error::Prod changes require 'allow-prod-change' label"
          exit 1
        fi
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions gate
name: Terraform Governance Check
on:
  pull_request:
    paths: ['**/*.tf']
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v2
      - name: Terraform Init
        run: terraform init
      - name: Terraform Plan
        run: terraform plan -out=tfplan
      - name: Validate Read-Only Data
        run: |
          if terraform show -json tfplan | jq -r '.configuration.root_module.resources[] | select(.mode == "data") | .type' | grep -q "terraform_remote_state"; then
            echo "✓ Read-only data bridge validated"
          else
            echo "✗ Missing required remote state data source"
            exit 1
          fi
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions sketch
name: Plan with Cost Gate
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v1
      - run: terraform init
      - run: terraform plan -out=tfplan
      - run: terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json
      - run: infracost breakdown --path plan.json
      - run: |
          BUDGET=100
          COST=$(infracost breakdown --path plan.json --format json | jq -r .timeframe[0].cost)
          if (( $(echo "$COST" > "$BUDGET" | bc -l) )); then exit 1; fi
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  B --> C[Budget check]
  C --> D[Apply if ok]
```
